text:
The keeper, Tomas, stood very still with his hand on the kettle. For three years the only sounds had been waves, wind, and his own voice. The knock came again, three slow taps, as if whoever was outside had all the time in the world.

He crossed the room and opened the door. On the step stood a girl of about nine, soaking wet, holding a brass lantern that was still lit. No boat sat on the rocks below. The tide had covered the causeway hours ago.

"Your light went out last night," she said. "I came to give you mine."

Tomas looked up at the tower. The great lamp was shining, as it had every night for three years. He turned back to say so, but the girl was already walking past him into the kitchen, and the lantern in her hand was burning with a flame the color of the sea.

Your turn. Who is she, and what is wrong with that flame?
